clue.text: Gymnast needs this money in the bank

definitions.meaning: a gymnast on the beam must keep their ..., their poise
a bank ... is the sum held in an account

explanation.surface: A gymnast is after a cash deposit rather than a steady footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Balance means both physical poise and the amount of funds held in an account.

clue.text: London 24 seen primarily in 3 on left

indicators.note: in tells us the chosen letter goes inside the word from the other entry

parts.note: the answer to 3 Down is ARENA

indicators.note: primarily asks for only the opening letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: A London football side shows up mostly in a stadium on the left side.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is ELEVEN, a football team, so the definition is a London club; 3 is the 3-down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous football club based in north London, so a London team of eleven players.

clue.text: Area near ground, or the ground itself

indicators.note: ground, as in crushed or milled, says the letters of near are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clarifies whether they mean the zone next to the stadium or the stadium proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' appears twice: first as the anagram signal (milled), then as a sports ground in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a sports stadium or enclosed venue, which is a ground in the sporting sense.

clue.text: Letter opposing drink

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against or opposing

explanation.surface: A letter of complaint is written against drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Decline what every player strives for

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a trophy is the prize every competitor hopes to win

explanation.surface: A player turns down the very prize they are chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer split as A TROPHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is wasting or deterioration, a gradual weakening; split in two it is the cup sportspeople chase.

clue.text: Golf supporter hires old character to produce choppers

indicators.note: hires means takes on, so the first word takes the second into its middle

parts.note: a tee holds up the golf ball
eth is an Old English letter

explanation.surface: A golf tee employs an old-timer to make some cutting tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is slang for teeth, and a baby who teethes is growing its first teeth.

clue.text: Location of member of 24's old theatre cutting

parts.note: NT stands for the National Theatre in London
hewing means cutting, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A footballer's old theatre is being trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is ELEVEN, a football team; a winger plays out on the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger in a football side plays out wide, so on the flank is where that player is found.

clue.text: Stealing possible contents of mound in Suffolk?

parts.note: Sutton Hoo in Suffolk is a famous Anglo-Saxon burial mound site, hoo being an old word for a spur of land
a king may have been buried in the ship burial there

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Suffolk mound might hold looted goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Sutton Hoo is a famous Anglo-Saxon royal burial site in Suffolk, England; a Hoo king is what it may contain.
explanation.definitionFit: To hook something is slang for to pinch or steal it, so hooking is thieving.

clue.text: Police aim to do this sport

definitions.meaning: police want to ..., crushing criminal schemes
the full name of the game of squash

explanation.surface: The police are said to be taking up a racquet game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rackets are crooked schemes that police crush, and squash rackets is a court game.

clue.text: Part of the Scillies, eastern half redeveloped

definitions.text: Part of the Scillies, eastern half redeveloped

indicators.note: redeveloped says those letters are rebuilt in a new order
in an across entry east is the right-hand side, so we keep the back four letters of the word

explanation.surface: Half of the Isles of Scilly is being redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern half' takes LIES from SCILLIES, and 'redeveloped' rearranges it. The Scillies are islands off Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scilly Isles are a group of small islands off south-west England, each one an island.

clue.text: Court investigation leader rejected for debate

parts.note: an inquest is a judicial inquiry, for instance into a death

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters for leader are read backwards

parts.note: a leader is No. 1, written NO I

explanation.surface: A court inquiry turns down its chairman, so the matter remains open.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is 'No. 1' in crossword shorthand, and 'rejected' turns those letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in question is one still under discussion and not yet settled.

clue.text: Useless way to carry goods I imported

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the letter goes inside the phrase

parts.note: goods may be carried in a van

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a goods route is pointless once they have brought it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in vain means done to no effect, which is futile or fruitless.

clue.text: Ultimately fit and lithe, trained in Air Corps

definitions.text: Ultimately fit and lithe, trained in Air Corps

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters sit inside the abbreviation
ultimately asks for only the final letter of the word fit
trained, as in drilled into shape, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruit ends up fit and supple after training in the Air Corps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' gives T and 'trained' rearranges LITHE to HLETI; both go 'in' AC. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic person is fit, strong and agile, exactly what such training produces.

clue.text: Boxer's cunning with rowers

definitions.note: read as Boxer is: the definition is a boxer and the 's is a link

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or cunning
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A boxer shows shrewdness in the company of oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in one of the lightest weight classes.

clue.text: Ring users with radical compounds, about 50

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for radical

indicators.note: about means going round, so the chemical word surrounds the numeral

parts.note: esters are organic chemical compounds
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: people using rings combine with radical compounds at around fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside ESTERS to make ESTLERS. 'Radical' and 'compounds' point to chemistry, but radical just gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestlers fight in a ring, so they are the people who use it.

clue.text: Some rubbing out needed in this game

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An eraser is required for playing this particular game.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'game'; 'needed in this' only links it to the wordplay, so the draft's longer definition is narrowed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game in which players mark off called numbers on a card.

clue.text: Comparatively adept sailor with large margins of error

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: margins of asks for only the outside letters of the word error

explanation.surface: A sailor with a wide margin for error is relatively skilful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'margins of' takes ER, the outside letters of 'error'; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, meaning more capable or skilled.

clue.text: A bit worried about old US lawman's CV?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the next pieces
worried means fretted at, so the letters are shaken up into a new order

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A little anxious about an elderly American lawman's résumé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is the anagram signal and 'about' is the container signal; the question mark admits that a CV is a loose match for this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Biodata is personal and career details, the same information a curriculum vitae gives.

clue.text: Button container that needs refilling regularly

definitions.text: Button container that needs refilling regularly

parts.words: Button container that needs refilling regularly
parts.note: Jenson Button was a Formula One driver, and his vehicle needed regular pit stops for fuel

explanation.surface: A box for buttons that must keep being topped up.
explanation.walkthrough: Button is Jenson Button, a British Formula One world champion; mid-race refuelling has since been banned in F1.
explanation.definitionFit: A Formula One vehicle carries the driver and, in his era, stopped to take on more fuel.

clue.text: Display of slippers rocks head office in Cornwall?

parts.note: drinks on the rocks are served with ice

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation goes inside the regional letters

parts.note: Cornwall is in south-west England, SW; the question mark admits the looseness

explanation.surface: A footwear display shakes a Cornish company's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippers' are skaters who slip on the ice, not footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice show is a performance by skaters, people gliding and sliding on ice.

clue.text: It's mean to state how old someone is

parts.note: to aver is to state or assert
a person's age is how old they are

explanation.surface: It is unkind to announce a person's age.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the usual average, the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: Crossing line, a bear raised game

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the reversed letters straddle the abbreviation
raised, in a down entry, means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: Pooh is Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear of A.A. Milne

explanation.surface: A bear crosses a line and is lifted up during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns A POOH upwards to HOOPA, and 'Crossing' puts it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground game where rings are thrown over prizes.

clue.text: Old couple in Split, dancing perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces go inside the word for split

parts.note: a fork is a split or branching
a couple is two

explanation.surface: An elderly pair in the Croatian city of Split, possibly dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split looks like the Croatian city, capitalised for the surface; it is a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwork is skilled movement of the feet, which dancing is an example of.

clue.text: Team in taxi missing reserves

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is the British army reserve; take it from taxi and the Roman numeral XI is left

explanation.surface: A team in a cab is short of substitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds XI, which is read as the number it stands for, as in a team sheet's First XI. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players, so a side is often called an eleven.

clue.text: Albatross beats this bird of prey

definitions.meaning: in golf an albatross, three under par, beats an ..., two under

explanation.surface: One bird outdoes a raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagle is both a golf score of two under par and a large hunting bird.

clue.text: A blend of chats and spiel?

definitions.text: A blend of chats and spiel?

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters of both words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A salesman's patter is a mixture of small talk and spiel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A blend of' mixes the letters of CHATS and SPIEL; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales pitch is a persuasive talk from a seller, chat and patter combined.

clue.text: A good service was one of her strengths

definitions.text: A good service was one of her strengths

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis player's strong serve is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: Steffi Graf was a German tennis champion; 'service' is the military RAF, not a serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf won many Grand Slam tennis titles, helped by a powerful serve.

clue.text: Robin's mate defending small member of 24 before change in terminology

definitions.text: member of 24 before change in terminology

indicators.note: defending means guarding, so the comic hero surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: Robin is Batman's sidekick

explanation.surface: Batman protects a small player before the jargon changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is ELEVEN, here a cricket team. Cricket's laws now say batter instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman is a cricketer who bats, the term used before the gender-neutral word batter.

clue.text: Son joins keener member of 24 at the back

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, so a keener is a weeper

explanation.surface: A son joins a more enthusiastic player in defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keener' looks like a comparative of keen but is a noun: one who keens, or mourns. 24 is ELEVEN, a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper is a football defender playing behind the back line.
